entities.name: Adam Konarski
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adam Konarski (1526–1581) was Bishop of Poznań from 1562 to 1574, one of the most consequential episodes in the diocese's history. His episcopate coincided with the height of the Reformation's impact on Poland — the period when Lutheranism, Calvinism, and the Polish Brethren (Socinians) achieved significant gains among the Polish nobility, and when the future of Catholicism in Poland was genuinely uncertain.

Konarski's tenure at Poznań placed him at the centre of the Polish Catholic Church's response to Protestantism. The Diocese of Poznań, covering one of Poland's most economically and culturally developed regions, included large numbers of Protestant nobility who had adopted Reformed faith. His pastoral and administrative response to this challenge had lasting consequences for the Polish Church's survival through the Reformation era.

His episcopate was also shaped by the broader Polish Reformation's distinctive character — Poland's famous 1573 Warsaw Confederation established a principle of religious tolerance almost unique in sixteenth-century Europe, making the Polish approach to religious plurality a model studied across the continent. Konarski's episcopate thus navigated the most complex period in the Polish Church's early modern history, contributing to the Catholic recovery under the Jesuits and the Tridentine reform that followed.
